newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk police defuse powerful bomb in train station.
newsitem.headline: Turk police defuse powerful bomb in train station.

text.p: Turkish police have defused a powerful bomb at a busy train station in Istanbul half an hour before it was due to go off, a rail official said on Tuesday.
"Police came and defused the bomb on Monday night after a warning call," the official at the Sirkeci station in the centre of the city told Reuters.

The bomb, left in a bag at a bank cash machine by unknown people, was timed to explode at 10 p.m. (2000 GMT) on Monday. The Turkish press said the device was found by passers-by who contacted the police.
The state-run Anatolian new agency said the 10-kg (22-lb) TNT bomb would have caused a major disaster if it had exploded.
Rebel Kurds, Islamist militants and leftist urban guerrillas have in the past staged bomb attacks on targets in Istanbul.
